C0.quote: each proposal k is decided through simple majority voting.
C0.note: The paper studies vote trading before majority voting on binary proposals, i.e. strategic aspects of a voting procedure.

C1.loc: Abstract, p.1; Section 2.3, p.7-8; Section 3.1.1, p.14-15
C1.quote: We explore this subject with a laboratory experiment.
C1.note: EQ: stability and convergence of Pivot algorithms (theorem from CP), which the conclusion calls an 'equilibrium concept based on stability'. SI: random-trading simulations used as a benchmark. Primary is the laboratory experiment.

C3.1.quote: pairs of voters exchange votes whenever doing so is mutually advantageous
C3.1.note: All analyses concern vote trading, which changes the votes submitted. Human subjects choose trades freely. Voting direction itself is sincere (dominant strategy, cast automatically).

C5.1.quote: Percentage of trades yielding farsighted gains and losses
C5.1.note: Trades and allocations are evaluated by traders' payoffs (payoff-improving trades, farsighted gains and losses).

C5.2.note: Utilities are computed from values z_ik, which are defined separately from vote holdings.

VOT.quote_behav: Pivot Algorithms are de…ned as sequences of trades yielding myopic strict gains
VOT.quote_info: The vote table conveys to all voters complete information about voters’preferences
VOT.note: Voters are myopically strategic traders in the theory, and lab subjects choose freely. The random-trading null benchmark is a comparison model, not the main behavioural model. Vote casting itself is sincere and automatic.

C8.1.note: DOM: sincere voting is a dominant strategy. ITER: Pivot algorithm of sequential myopic improving trades. COAL: pairwise stability and the farsighted core / F-dominance.
